case_title.quote: MAJOR SINGH v. STATE OF PUNJAB & ANR.
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: There is only one accused and one injury was given by the accused.
number_of_accused.reason: Judgment states there is only one accused.

accused_gender.quote: the appellant ... who is real nephew of the deceased
accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to with male pronouns and as a nephew.

accused_age.reason: No age for the appellant appears anywhere in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation of the accused is not mentioned.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: Makhan Singh, father of Sukhraj Singh (complainant)
victim_gender.reason: Victim is a male uncle, referred to as father and with male pronouns.

victim_age.reason: Judgment describes the victim as old and feeble but gives no age of 65.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused was the nephew of the deceased uncle.

offence_category.reason: Final conviction is for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s.302 (High Court conviction); s.304 Part-II (Supreme Court conviction); s.300 Exception 4 considered
statutory_provisions.quote: The appellant is convicted under Section 304 Part-II IPC.
statutory_provisions.reason: Omits s.302 under which the High Court convicted and the Exception 4 argument.

weapon.quote: holding a wooden 'Bahi' (wooden side of a cot frame)
weapon.reason: Weapon is the wooden cot leg, called Bahi, and was recovered.

evidence_type.quote: the main injury was on the head ... both the eye witnesses ... The recovery of 'Bahi'
evidence_type.reason: Medical, eyewitness and recovery evidence are all relied on.

confession.quote: he confessed about the concealment of 'Bahi' by him in the wheat chaff room
confession.reason: Confession about hiding the Bahi is recorded, and the Bahi was recovered.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: High Court noted blow with great force on head of an old and feeble man, and grudge from previous quarrel
aggravating_circumstances.quote: the manner in which the appellant gave a blow of wooden arm of cot ('Bahi') with great force on the head of an old and feeble man
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Judgment records aggravating points considered by the High Court, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Provocation by uncle's reprimand the previous day; single blow; non-dangerous weapon; no intention to kill
mitigating_circumstances.quote: He was furious about getting yelled by his uncle a day before, which acted as a provocation
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Judgment expressly lists provocation, single blow and non-dangerous weapon as mitigating points.

trial_court_outcome.quote: The learned Additional Sessions Judge, Muktsar vide order 13.07.2001, acquitted the appellant

high_court_outcome.quote: the appellant was convicted under section 302 IPC
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court convicted under s.302 IPC.

final_outcome.quote: the Appeals are partly allowed. The judgment of the High Court is modified
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court partly allowed appeal and modified the conviction.

offence_finally_established.quote: the deceased is not liable to be convicted under section 302 IPC but would be liable to be convicted under section 304 Part-II IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Final established offence is culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

imprisonment_type.correct_value: Sentence of period already undergone (time served), not a stated fixed term
imprisonment_type.quote: awarded sentence of the period already undergone
imprisonment_type.reason: Sentence is time already served; 'fixed_term' is an inference the judgment does not state.

imprisonment_years.correct_value: More than eight years (period already undergone)
imprisonment_years.quote: He has already undergone more than eight years of incarceration.
imprisonment_years.reason: Judgment says more than eight years, not exactly 8, and sentence is time served.

fine_rs.reason: High Court fine of Rs.5,000 was retained, so null is wrong.

neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate and do not reveal the Supreme Court outcome.

offence_severity.reason: No severity rating is stated in the judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: The deceased died due to the injury caused by accused.
attempt_completion.reason: Offence was completed with death of the victim.

physical_harm.quote: the cause of death was due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of head injury
physical_harm.reason: Eight injuries, main head injury, and death from shock and haemorrhage are stated.

number_of_offences.correct_value: One offence; charged and convicted by High Court under s.302 IPC; Supreme Court convicted under s.304 Part-II
number_of_offences.quote: the appellant was convicted under section 302 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Value wrongly says High Court convicted under s.304; it was s.302.

financial_property_loss.reason: No financial or property loss is mentioned, so the not-applicable value fits.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Supreme Court did not expressly find no premeditation; High Court held the attack was not sudden and arose from a grudge
premeditation_planning.quote: the occurrence had not taken place all of a sudden and without any predetermination
premeditation_planning.reason: Supreme Court does not expressly find lack of premeditation; High Court reasoning points the other way.

motive.quote: Maybe he wanted to punish his uncle for the reprimand, he received the previous day.
motive.reason: Motive of punishing the uncle for the reprimand is stated, though tentatively.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: The recovery of 'Bahi', i.e. the weapon used to cause the fatal injury
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Post-mortem, eyewitness and weapon recovery evidence were accepted as established.

witness_credibility.correct_value: High Court found the ocular version truthful and trustworthy, supported by medical evidence; trial court had found eyewitnesses not credible
witness_credibility.quote: Ocular version is truthful and trust worthy and is fully supported by the medical evidence.
witness_credibility.reason: This is the High Court's finding, not the Supreme Court's, and the trial court had disbelieved the witnesses.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Ran away from the spot after the blow; surrendered after the High Court conviction on 04.10.2014
post_offence_conduct.quote: Major Singh ran away from the spot with the 'Bahi'
post_offence_conduct.reason: Surrender is correct, but the flight from the spot is omitted.

custody_duration.correct_value: Arrested 09.08.1998; released 13.07.2001 after acquittal; re-surrendered 04.10.2014; over eight years incarceration
custody_duration.quote: The appellant was arrested on 09.08.1998 and was released on 13.07.2001
custody_duration.reason: Judgment states custody dates and total incarceration, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

bail_history.reason: Bail is not mentioned; release followed acquittal and is not described as bail.

trial_duration.reason: Offence, trial, High Court and Supreme Court dates match the judgment.

legal_representation.quote: Gagan Gupta, Adv. for the Appellant. R. K. Rathore, Ms. Jaspreet Gogia, Advs. for the Respondents.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered; police investigation with site plan and recovery; case committed to Sessions Court 13.10.1998; trial completed
investigation_status.quote: the case was committed to the Sessions Court, vide order dated 13.10.1998
investigation_status.reason: A charge sheet filing is not expressly stated; committal to Sessions Court is recorded.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Trial court noted 4½-hour FIR delay and late arrest; High Court held these not fatal
procedural_irregularity.quote: There was a delay of 4½ hours in recording the FIR.
procedural_irregularity.reason: Irregularities were raised by the trial court, though the High Court found them not material.

appeal_history.quote: the appeal and revision petition were allowed, the acquittal by the Trial Court was set aside
appeal_history.reason: Trial acquittal, High Court conviction under s.302, and Supreme Court modification match.

prosecution_argument.quote: the death of the deceased was homicidal
prosecution_argument.reason: Summary of prosecution case on homicide, eyewitnesses, post-mortem and recovery is supported.

defence_argument.correct_value: Counsel pleaded in the alternative for culpable homicide not amounting to murder (s.304); accused claimed false implication
defence_argument.quote: as has been pleaded by the counsel for the appellant in the alternative
defence_argument.reason: Lack of intention and weapon points are the court's reasoning, not recorded defence arguments.

legal_principle_applied.quote: Intention is pivotal to decide whether the accused has committed culpable homicide amounting to murder
legal_principle_applied.reason: Accurately reflects the intention, knowledge and degree test applied.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Mohd. Rafiq v. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2021) 10 SCC 706 – referred to.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: s.304 Part-II chosen for lack of intention to kill and single blow; sentence reduced because more than eight years already undergone
sentencing_rationale.quote: His sentence shall be reduced from life imprisonment to period already undergone.
sentencing_rationale.reason: Omits the custody-period reason for reducing the sentence.

judicial_mitigating_factors.correct_value: Provocation by previous day's reprimand; lack of intention; single blow; non-dangerous weapon
judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: He was furious about getting yelled by his uncle a day before, which acted as a provocation
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Lack of premeditation is not listed as a mitigating factor by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Supreme Court identifies no aggravating factors; High Court's aggravating points are not adopted.

other_sentence_order.quote: The appellant may be released forthwith, if he is not wanted in any other criminal case. ... fine imposed by the High Court would remain as it is.
other_sentence_order.reason: Sentence reduction, release and fine retention are accurately stated.
